input: This capital appraisal considers a proposed warehouse extension and sets out the financial figures that have been assembled in support of the investment. The installed cost of the extension has been put at $485k, and the expected net saving has been estimated at $117k per year over a period of 8 years. Using a discount rate of 10%, the present value of the savings works out at $624k, which in turn gives a net present value of $139k for the project as a whole. On the face of it, this is a positive result, since the present value of the savings, at $624k, exceeds the installed cost of $485k by a comfortable margin. It is important to note, however, that the savings underpinning this appraisal are vendor and utility estimates, and no saving of this kind has yet been measured on a comparable installation, so there is inevitably a degree of uncertainty surrounding the saving figure. Decision-makers will therefore wish to consider not only the headline net present value of $139k, but also the basis on which the expected net saving of $117k per year for 8 years has been arrived at, before reaching a final view.
target: Recommendation: proceed with the warehouse extension, on the strength of the appraisal and with its basis stated plainly. The installed cost is $485k. The expected net saving is $117k per year for 8 years. At a discount rate of 10%, the present value of the savings is $624k, and the net present value is $139k. The margin is the difference between the two present figures: savings worth $624k in present terms against an installed cost of $485k, a difference in the project's favour. The basis of the appraisal is estimates. The savings are vendor and utility estimates, and no saving has yet been measured on a comparable installation, so the net present value of $139k is an appraised figure whose accuracy is the accuracy of estimates that have never been checked against a measured case. The decision the figures support is approval of the warehouse extension as appraised. They do not remove the need to treat the $117k per year as an estimate in the first years of operation, to compare the measured saving against it year by year over the 8 years, and to hold the appraisal answerable to that comparison. The appraisal period and the discounting are stated on the face of the figures, and the recommendation accepts both as given; what the recommendation does not accept without remark is the habit of treating an estimate as though it were a measurement.
